questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why the dodo became extinct on its island
How to survive a natural disaster like a flood
The biggest dangers to humanity and if we'll survive
The history of the Cold War between the US and Russia
questions.why: Neil says they'll look at dangers facing humanity and whether civilisation can survive them.

questions.q: Why did the dodo die out, according to the presenters?
options: It was hunted by humans and didn't hide from them
Its island home was destroyed by a volcano
It caught a deadly disease from the sailors' dogs
Its main food ran out after a long, dry summer
questions.why: Neil says dodos couldn't fly, didn't hide from sailors with dogs, and were hunted to extinction.

questions.q: Why does Neil disagree that humans are too clever to die out?
options: Humans are not as clever as we think
Humans are losing interest in science
The Earth is getting too hot to live on
Many of the biggest risks are made by humans
questions.why: He says lots of existential risks, like nuclear war or rogue AI, are human-made.

questions.q: According to Simon Beard, what happens about once every thousand years?
options: A giant asteroid hits the Earth and kills many
An event wipes out about a third of the population
A completely new species of animal appears
A nuclear war begins between two superpowers
questions.why: He says about once every thousand years an event wipes out about a third of the human population.

questions.q: What example does Simon Beard give from the Middle Ages?
options: A great flood that covered much of Europe
A long war between England and France
The Black Death and global cooling
A terrible famine in Africa and Asia
questions.why: He mentions the Black Death and dramatic global cooling, possibly linked to volcanoes.

questions.q: According to Seth Baum, how could a nuclear war start without anyone intending it?
options: Through a computer virus
Through a false alarm mistaken for an attack
Through a terrorist stealing a bomb
Through an accident at a power station
questions.why: He says the biggest example is a false alarm that is mistaken as a nuclear attack.

options: The US and Russia signed an important peace deal
A nuclear bomb exploded by accident in a desert
A deadly pandemic spread quickly around the world
Soviet radars mistook US science rockets for an attack
questions.why: Sam says US missiles sent up to study the northern lights were mistaken for nuclear warheads.

questions.q: What hopeful idea does Neil suggest at the end?
options: Human intelligence could also solve the problems we made
Humans could all move to a safe desert island
The dangers have all been greatly exaggerated by the media
Nuclear weapons will soon disappear from the world
questions.why: He says the same intelligence which split the atom could find solutions to our human-made problems.
